shell-injected-env: The sidecar process this TS ran in carried GAMELIB_SHELL_EXE, GAMELIB_APP_ROOT, GAMELIB_STEAM_ROOT_DEFAULT and GAMELIB_STORE_BOOT, injected by src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs. A spawn from the shell own environment does not carry them, so the Rust runner env is the golden env without those four keys. No golden here holds them (the cases run on the pinned base env), so the Rust side adds none and the delta only records the rule for the cases that compare against a sidecar-run recording.
caller-arrays-mutated: The TS runWineCommand changes the arrays its caller handed it: commandParts gains the proton verb, the wrappers and the runner bin in place, and options.wrappers loses its first element to the spawned binary (commandPartsAfter, wrappersAfter in result.json). The Rust function takes its arguments by value and builds the argv on its own copy, so the Rust side compares the spawned argv and leaves both lists as the caller had them.
error-stack-trace: A launch script that fails to spawn is logged by runScriptForGame as the Error itself, and the TS log writer stringifies it with its JS stack (frames naming src/backend files and node_modules). The golden keeps the first line, "Error: spawn <script> <code>", and drops the "    at ..." lines, which name the machine and the test runner. The Rust runner logs the spawn error message and has no JS stack, so the comparison is on the first line only.
wine-path-error-line: The TS getWinePath logged an error line carrying the path asked about and the standard error of winepath ("Couldn't get wine path for <path>.\n<stderr>"), and the golden events hold it. Both can name a profile path, so the Rust op answers 88.1-13's get_wine_path, whose empty-answer line is the fixed text "Couldn't get wine path" (prohibition 1: no gamelib.log line carries a path or a profile path). The line is written for exactly the cases the TS wrote it for (an empty answer), and golden_wine_path compares that fixed text.
wine-path-log-lines: The TS getWinePath wrote a debug line "Getting wine path for <path>." and runWineCommand wrote "Running Wine command: <parts>" (the winepath arguments, with the path), the first two events of every golden. Both carry the path asked about, and 88.1-13's get_wine_path (which the op answers through) writes neither: it runs 87's run_wine_command, which logs no run line. golden_wine_path compares nothing at debug level and asserts no warning or error line carries the path.
wine-path-track-and-resolve-on: The TS runWineCommand registered the winepath child under track { runner: 'wine', key: <prefix> } and resolved on 'close' (the track and resolveOn fields of every spawn in the goldens). 88.1-13's get_wine_path runs 87's run_wine_command, the same delta 87 recorded for wine_command (track-and-resolve-on): the child is a Helper ended by the cancel token and the shutdown token, with the spawn seam's own drain. A winepath answers in milliseconds and nothing kills a prefix's tracked children while one runs, so no behaviour is lost; the launch variant (88.2-12) is what registers a launch's wine command. The spawn (program, argv, whole env, cwd, replaceEnv, timeout, class) is the golden's.
